text: Marie Curie was a physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity, a term she coined. Born Maria Sklodowska in Warsaw in 1867, she later moved to Paris to study at the University of Paris. Together with her husband Pierre Curie, she discovered the elements polonium and radium. She won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903, shared with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, and then won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911, becoming the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields. During the First World War she developed mobile X ray units to help treat wounded soldiers. She died in 1934 from aplastic anaemia, likely caused by her long exposure to radiation.

The Airbus A320 is a family of narrow body airliners developed and manufactured by Airbus. The A320 was the first commercial aircraft to feature a digital fly by wire flight control system, in which pilot inputs are transmitted electronically rather than through mechanical linkages. It entered service in 1988 with Air France. The aircraft typically seats between 140 and 170 passengers and has a range of about 6,100 kilometres. The A320 family includes shorter and longer variants known as the A318, A319, and A321. It is one of the best selling airliner families in history and is a direct competitor to the Boeing 737.

Redis is an open source, in memory data structure store used as a database, cache, and message broker. It was created by Salvatore Sanfilippo and first released in 2009. Unlike traditional databases that store data primarily on disk, Redis keeps the entire dataset in memory, which allows for very low latency reads and writes. It supports a range of data structures including strings, hashes, lists, sets, and sorted sets. Redis provides optional persistence by periodically writing snapshots to disk or by appending each write operation to a log. It is commonly used to cache the results of expensive database queries and to store user session data in web applications.

Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti inflammatory drug commonly used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain from conditions such as headaches, menstrual cramps, and arthritis. It works by inhibiting enzymes known as cyclooxygenases, which reduces the production of prostaglandins that cause inflammation and pain. Ibuprofen is available over the counter in many countries and was first marketed in 1969. Common side effects include stomach upset and, with prolonged use, an increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding. It is generally advised to take ibuprofen with food to reduce stomach irritation. The medication is not recommended during the later stages of pregnancy.

Lisbon is the capital and largest city of Portugal, situated on the Atlantic coast where the Tagus River meets the ocean. It is one of the oldest cities in Western Europe, predating other modern capitals such as London and Paris by centuries. The city is built across seven hills, which makes many of its streets steep and winding. Lisbon has a mild Mediterranean climate, with warm dry summers and cool rainy winters. Its historic tram network, especially the yellow Route 28 tram, is a well known feature. The 1755 Lisbon earthquake destroyed much of the city and led to a major rebuilding of the downtown Baixa district in a grid pattern.
